newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury workers in Bournville strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury workers in Bournville strike vote.

text.p: Workers at Cadbury Schweppes plc's Bournville plant voted 474 to 178 in favour of strike action over the company's proposed change in shift hours, said Doug Lee, a works convenor for the Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU).

Lee said on Wednesday the union was now in the process of officially notifying the company of what action the union plans to take and when, which should take about a week. He estimated 750 people would walk out, which he said could affect production "because we are the chocolate producers and we make chocolate for other factories."
A Cadbury spokesman declined to comment on whether production would be affected but said the strike threat was localised only in Bournville's moulded factory.

The dispute centres around accrued hours, Lee said. Currently, he said workers have a 168-hour shift, or 42-hour week. But they are only paid for a 39-hour week. Cadbury's compensates for the three hours by allowing workers to accrue the hours and either take time off in lieu when they wish or get extra pay.
But now, Lee said the company wants to abolish that system and offer fixed days off. He said Cadbury's was offering 10 fixed days off next year and 12 the following year.
"They are trying to tell them (the workers) what to do with the hours," Lee said.

Cadbury said in a statement "although we await official notice, we are disappointed by the apparent outcome of the ballot because we believe these improvements to the shift pattern are necessary in order to maximize future plant performance. We will evaluate the situation and consider how best to move forward."
